clue.text: Primarily grand, imposing, regal — a fine, furry East African native

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

blocks.clueFragment: grand, imposing, regal — a fine, furry East
blocks.note: the initial letters of these seven words

explanation.surface: A description of some grand, regal, furry beast native to East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface itself describes the animal, so the opening letters spell the very creature being pictured.
explanation.definitionFit: The tallest land mammal is found wild only on that continent, a creature that lives there by birth.

indicators.note: not tells the solver to leave out the following letter from the word before

blocks.note: a long slender sea fish with a beak-like snout
f is forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A nonsense riddle about a fish that is somehow both loud and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: GARFISH without its F leaves GARISH; the repeated words make the clue look like a tongue-twister.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish colours or clothes are showy and glaring, which in fashion talk is called loud.

blocks.note: red is the colour of left-wing politics
an act of parliament is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: Someone is told to amend a left-wing government's laws.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact a document is to prepare it for publication by cutting or censoring parts of it.

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so these letters are not in their true order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business statement that the gains reported are genuine, not misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not false' reads as 'true', but 'not' is part of the fodder and 'false' alone mixes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks left by feet pressed into mud or sand are impressions in the literal physical sense.

blocks.note: first meaning: an additional one
second meaning: a performer hired to appear in the background of a film

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that look like 'one more performer' are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An additional item is an extra, and a non-speaking crowd performer in films is also called that.

blocks.note: first meaning: peaceful, wanting no war
second meaning: the largest body of water on Earth

explanation.walkthrough: The ocean was named by Magellan for its calm waters, so both senses share one root.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific means peaceable or calm, and it is also the name of the world's biggest sea.

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

blocks.note: a principle is a fundamental rule

explanation.surface: A headmaster publicly declares a new school regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: The two spellings sound the same: a rule is a principle, a school head is a principal.
explanation.definitionFit: In American and some British colleges the person in charge of the institution has that title.

blocks.note: first meaning: is unable, written with an apostrophe
second meaning: insincere pious talk

explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords ignore apostrophes, so the contraction for 'cannot' counts as the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is sanctimonious, insincere talk about morals, which is a form of hypocrisy.

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone went in search of properly prepared meals.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone is to go behind them, so both phrases describe pursuing in the past tense.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the second

blocks.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
a television set

explanation.surface: A class discusses a recording made from the TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a small plastic case holding magnetic recording tape for audio or video.

indicators.note: in places the preceding word inside the one that follows

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port
to plug a product is to advertise it, and an ad is the result

explanation.surface: Instructions to connect a wireless gadget by plugging it into a socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' and 'port' look like computer hardware, but one is advertising and the other a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless is the old-fashioned British term for a broadcast receiver set.

blocks.note: surface reading: romance and a holiday island
setter's reading: two words that each come before the same three-sided shape in a familiar phrase

explanation.walkthrough: A love triangle involves three people; the Bermuda Triangle is the stretch of sea where ships are said to vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Each word is the first half of a well-known phrase ending in the plural geometric figure being asked for.

clue.text: Weirdly a NYC psycho is licking boots

indicators.note: weirdly means in a strange way, so the letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A New York madman is strangely fawning over someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootlicking is the idiom for grovelling flattery of the powerful, which is what toadying servility means.

indicators.note: a bit means only a portion, here a run of letters lying across two words

blocks.note: the letters straddling the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A cable car's doors open slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable car' reads as one thing, but the clue splits after 'Cable', which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick strong cord made of twisted strands is a cable, a synonym for heavy cord.

clue.text: In credit briefly and relaxing on the way up

blocks.note: taken as written
CR is the standard abbreviation for credit on a bank statement
easing off means relaxing

explanation.surface: A person in the black and taking it easy as things improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way up' could be a reversal signal in a down clue; here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something growing or rising in amount is climbing, the idiom being a way of saying it mounts.

clue.text: Dine out, sitting next to writer with depression — that's unconnected

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the preceding letters are rearranged
sitting next to means placed alongside, so the pieces join end to end

blocks.note: taken as written
a pen writes
a dent is a hollow or depression; with joins it on

explanation.surface: Eating out beside a gloomy author leaves you feeling cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood, but it is a physical hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something independent is free-standing and not attached or linked to anything else.

indicators.note: interfering means meddling and disrupting, so the letters get thoroughly mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Disturbances disrupting detectives as they reach their conclusions in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is a conclusion reached by a jury or judge, so each one is a ruling made.

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the next word's letters are put together anew
chasing means following behind, so the first piece goes after the second

blocks.note: taken as written
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A pal pursuing a construction company for a price for the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building site' reads as one phrase, but 'building' is the anagram signal for the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman's quotation is a stated rough price for a job, given before the work begins.

indicators.note: in places the preceding word inside the one that follows

blocks.note: a deed is a signed legal contract
a feat is a notable achievement

explanation.surface: Someone was outdone by a clause in a legal agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be defeated is to have lost a contest, the same as being overcome or vanquished.

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the preceding letters are in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An amazing performer tidies up after the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clears up mess' reads as tidying, but 'mess' is the signal and 'clears up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spectacular is so impressive or striking that it takes your breath away.

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
Cate Blanchett, the Australian actress

explanation.surface: Look at the place where the actress Cate Blanchett is.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to find or pinpoint it, which is what it means to locate it.

clue.text: Look what you may get, if you bend down in an American  henhouse, say!

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the phrase, using its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.clueFragment: what you may get, if you bend down in an American  henhouse
blocks.note: bending over among hens, your American rear would be pecked

explanation.surface: A comic warning about what happens if you stoop in a chicken coop.
explanation.walkthrough: Ass is the American word for backside; spoken, the phrase for having it pecked matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the look or appearance of something, as in a building's sunny outlook.

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the preceding word is read from its end

blocks.note: the compiler of the crossword speaks of themself as I
to meet a need is to satisfy it

explanation.surface: The setter is happy with some fine point.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves as 'compiler', 'setter' or 'this writer', all giving I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a single particular, one item in a list or account.

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters are relocated into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Boxes being shifted along with the stairs during a house move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' appears twice: first as the anagram signal, then inside the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Escalators are staircases whose treads travel up or down powered by a motor.

clue.text: Relatives value notes being regularly sent off

indicators.note: regularly sent off means every other letter is dismissed, keeping the remainder

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Family members' banknotes are being posted off at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Your parents' sisters are family members, so they count among your kin.

blocks.note: first meaning: Sir Christopher, designer of St Paul's Cathedral in London
second meaning: a tiny brown songbird

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive suggests a bird belonging to an architect; the 's is just 'is' joining two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher of that surname was the great English architect, and the same word names a small songbird.

indicators.note: misrepresented means presented wrongly, so the letters are given in a false order

blocks.note: taken as written
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper, or perhaps none at all, gave a false picture of the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is the abbreviation for post meridiem.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, labels the hours after midday, the part of the day after noon.

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the answer is formed from letters within the following words

blocks.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A painting showing a man growing old, like Dorian Gray's.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a picture or likeness of a person, so it is a representation of them.

clue.text: The musician honoured Rossini in playing his finales

indicators.note: finales are the closing parts, so the last letter of each word is kept

blocks.clueFragment: The musician honoured Rossini in playing his
blocks.note: the final letters of these seven words

explanation.surface: A performer paid tribute to the composer by playing the closing sections of his operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finales' does double duty, telling you to take last letters and defining the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a piece or show, so finales are its concluding sections.

clue.text: Part of pants (eg gusset) turns intimate

indicators.note: part of means only a portion of the following words is used
turns means flips around, so the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word into the last, before it is flipped

explanation.surface: Some saucy talk about underwear, its gusset becoming something private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' looks like an adjective about underwear, but here it is the verb meaning to hint.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate something is to hint at it indirectly, which is to propose it without saying outright.
